10:1.sourceText: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὁ μὴ εἰσερχόμενος διὰ τῆς θύρας εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τῶν προβάτων ἀλλὰ ἀναβαίνων ἀλλαχόθεν, ἐκεῖνος κλέπτης ἐστὶν καὶ λῃστής·
10:1.targetText: “Truly, truly, I say to you, he who is not entering through the door to the fold of the sheep, but is going up from another side, that one is a thief and a robber;

10:2.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἰσερχόμενος διὰ τῆς θύρας ποιμήν ἐστιν τῶν προβάτων.
10:2.targetText: and he who is entering through the door is shepherd of the sheep;

10:3.sourceText: τούτῳ ὁ θυρωρὸς ἀνοίγει, καὶ τὰ πρόβατα τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούει, καὶ τὰ ἴδια πρόβατα φωνεῖ κατ’ ὄνομα καὶ ἐξάγει αὐτά.
10:3.targetText: the doorkeeper opens to this one, and the sheep hear his voice, and his own sheep he calls by name, and leads them forth;

10:4.sourceText: ὅταν τὰ ἴδια πάντα ἐκβάλῃ, ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν πορεύεται, καὶ τὰ πρόβατα αὐτῷ ἀκολουθεῖ, ὅτι οἴδασιν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ·
10:4.targetText: and when he may put forth his own sheep, he goes on before them, and the sheep follow him, because they have known his voice;

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness difference: N1904 explicitly has πάντα (all) with his own; LSV instead names sheep without separately expressing all.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV begins and; pinned N1904 starts directly ὅταν (when) with no conjunction.
Source witness difference: LSV explicitly names his own sheep; N1904 has τὰ ἴδια πάντα (all his own) with no sheep noun in the first clause.

10:5.sourceText: ἀλλοτρίῳ δὲ οὐ μὴ ἀκολουθήσουσιν, ἀλλὰ φεύξονται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδασιν τῶν ἀλλοτρίων τὴν φωνήν.
10:5.targetText: and they will not follow a stranger, but will flee from him, because they have not known the voice of strangers.”

10:6.sourceText: Ταύτην τὴν παροιμίαν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· ἐκεῖνοι δὲ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τίνα ἦν ἃ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς.
10:6.targetText: Jesus spoke this allegory to them, and they did not know what the things were that He was speaking to them;

10:7.sourceText: Εἶπεν οὖν πάλιν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα τῶν προβάτων.
10:7.targetText: Jesus therefore said again to them, “Truly, truly, I say to you, I AM the door of the sheep;

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces I AM the door; LSV gives direct speech without a separate that.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV includes to them after the introductory said again; N1904 has no corresponding recipient pronoun there.

10:8.sourceText: πάντες ὅσοι ἦλθον πρὸ ἐμοῦ κλέπται εἰσὶν καὶ λῃσταί· ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἤκουσαν αὐτῶν τὰ πρόβατα.
10:8.targetText: all, as many as came before Me, are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not hear them;

10:9.sourceText: ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα· δι’ ἐμοῦ ἐάν τις εἰσέλθῃ, σωθήσεται, καὶ εἰσελεύσεται καὶ ἐξελεύσεται καὶ νομὴν εὑρήσει.
10:9.targetText: I AM the door, if anyone may come in through Me, he will be saved, and he will come in, and go out, and find pasture.

10:10.sourceText: ὁ κλέπτης οὐκ ἔρχεται εἰ μὴ ἵνα κλέψῃ καὶ θύσῃ καὶ ἀπολέσῃ· ἐγὼ ἦλθον ἵνα ζωὴν ἔχωσιν καὶ περισσὸν ἔχωσιν.
10:10.targetText: The thief does not come, except that he may steal, and kill, and destroy; I came that they may have life, and may have [it] abundantly.

unmappedTarget.reason: Translation addition: LSV repeats the understood life object in brackets; N1904 has no object pronoun with the second have verb.

10:11.sourceText: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός. ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλὸς τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ τίθησιν ὑπὲρ τῶν προβάτων·
10:11.targetText: I AM the good shepherd; the good shepherd lays His life down for the sheep;

10:12.sourceText: ὁ μισθωτὸς καὶ οὐκ ὢν ποιμήν, οὗ οὐκ ἔστιν τὰ πρόβατα ἴδια, θεωρεῖ τὸν λύκον ἐρχόμενον καὶ ἀφίησιν τὰ πρόβατα καὶ φεύγει,— καὶ ὁ λύκος ἁρπάζει αὐτὰ καὶ σκορπίζει·—
10:12.targetText: and the hired worker, and not being a shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, beholds the wolf coming, and leaves the sheep, and flees; and the wolf snatches them, and scatters the sheep;

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV begins and; N1904 starts directly ὁ μισθωτός without an initial conjunction.
Source witness difference: LSV repeats the sheep as the object of scatters; N1904 has no sheep noun after σκορπίζει.

10:13.sourceText: ὅτι μισθωτός ἐστιν καὶ οὐ μέλει αὐτῷ περὶ τῶν προβάτων.
10:13.targetText: and the hired worker flees because he is a hired worker, and is not caring for the sheep.

groups.note: Greek οὐ μέλει αὐτῷ is impersonal (it is no concern to him); LSV is not caring expresses the same personal indifference. The full idiom is paired without claiming the same grammatical subject.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV repeats the subject and fleeing verb at the start of this verse; N1904 begins directly because he is a hired worker with no such repeated clause.

10:14.sourceText: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, καὶ γινώσκω τὰ ἐμὰ καὶ γινώσκουσί με τὰ ἐμά,
10:14.targetText: I AM the good shepherd, and I know My [sheep], and am known by Mine,

unmappedTarget.reason: Translation addition: LSV supplies sheep in brackets with the substantival My own phrase; N1904 has τὰ ἐμά without a sheep noun here.

review.note: N1904 says My own know Me with an active third-person-plural verb and explicit Me object; LSV am known by Mine follows the passive wording. The same knowing relationship and participants are preserved through the voice shift, without claiming identical inflection.

10:15.sourceText: καθὼς γινώσκει με ὁ Πατὴρ κἀγὼ γινώσκω τὸν Πατέρα, καὶ τὴν ψυχήν μου τίθημι ὑπὲρ τῶν προβάτων.
10:15.targetText: according as the Father knows Me, and I know the Father, and My life I lay down for the sheep,

10:16.sourceText: καὶ ἄλλα πρόβατα ἔχω ἃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τῆς αὐλῆς ταύτης· κἀκεῖνα δεῖ με ἀγαγεῖν, καὶ τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούσουσιν, καὶ γενήσεται μία ποίμνη, εἷς ποιμήν.
10:16.targetText: and other sheep I have that are not of this fold, these also it is necessary for Me to bring, and My voice they will hear, and there will become one flock—one shepherd.

10:17.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτό με ὁ Πατὴρ ἀγαπᾷ ὅτι ἐγὼ τίθημι τὴν ψυχήν μου, ἵνα πάλιν λάβω αὐτήν.
10:17.targetText: Because of this the Father loves Me, because I lay down My life, that again I may take it;

10:18.sourceText: οὐδεὶς ἦρεν αὐτὴν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ τίθημι αὐτὴν ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ. ἐξουσίαν ἔχω θεῖναι αὐτήν, καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχω πάλιν λαβεῖν αὐτήν· ταύτην τὴν ἐντολὴν ἔλαβον παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός μου.
10:18.targetText: no one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of Myself; authority I have to lay it down, and authority I have again to take it; this command I received from My Father.”

groups.note: N1904 ἦρεν is aorist (took/has taken), while LSV takes follows the present αἴρει reading. The take lexeme is shared without claiming identical tense.

10:19.sourceText: Σχίσμα πάλιν ἐγένετο ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις διὰ τοὺς λόγους τούτους.
10:19.targetText: Therefore, again, there came a division among the Jews, because of these words,

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV begins Therefore; N1904 has no οὖν or corresponding inference word here.

10:20.sourceText: ἔλεγον δὲ πολλοὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν Δαιμόνιον ἔχει καὶ μαίνεται· τί αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε;
10:20.targetText: and many of them said, “He has a demon, and is mad, why do you hear Him?”

10:21.sourceText: ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα οὐκ ἔστιν δαιμονιζομένου· μὴ δαιμόνιον δύναται τυφλῶν ὀφθαλμοὺς ἀνοῖξαι;
10:21.targetText: Others said, “These sayings are not those of a demoniac; is a demon able to open blind men’s eyes?”

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μή marks negative expectation; LSV is a demon able has no separate negative particle.

10:22.sourceText: Ἐγένετο τότε τὰ ἐνκαίνια ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις· χειμὼν ἦν·
10:22.targetText: And the Dedication in Jerusalem came, and it was winter,

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness connective difference: N1904 has τότε (then), while LSV begins And, corresponding to δέ in the TR reading.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness connective difference: LSV begins And; N1904 has temporal τότε (then), not the same additive word.
Source witness/coordination difference: LSV connects the winter clause with and; N1904 begins χειμὼν ἦν directly without a corresponding conjunction.

10:23.sourceText: καὶ περιεπάτει ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐν τῇ στοᾷ τοῦ Σολομῶνος.
10:23.targetText: and Jesus was walking in the temple, in the porch of Solomon,

10:24.sourceText: ἐκύκλωσαν οὖν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ Ἕως πότε τὴν ψυχὴν ἡμῶν αἴρεις; εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστός, εἰπὸν ἡμῖν παρρησίᾳ.
10:24.targetText: the Jews, therefore, came around Him and said to Him, “Until when do You hold our soul in suspense? If You are the Christ, tell us freely.”

targetPhrases.text: do You hold our soul in suspense

groups.note: The Greek lift/take-our-soul idiom asks about keeping the speakers in suspense. Its full four-token constituent is paired to the English idiom; αἴρω alone is not assigned the general meaning hold in suspense.

10:25.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἶπον ὑμῖν, καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε· τὰ ἔργα ἃ ἐγὼ ποιῶ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Πατρός μου, ταῦτα μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ·
10:25.targetText: Jesus answered them, “I told you, and you do not believe; the works that I do in the Name of My Father, these testify concerning Me;

10:26.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετε, ὅτι οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐκ τῶν προβάτων τῶν ἐμῶν.
10:26.targetText: but you do not believe, for you are not of My sheep,

10:27.sourceText: τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἐμὰ τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούουσιν, κἀγὼ γινώσκω αὐτά, καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσίν μοι,
10:27.targetText: according as I said to you: My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me,

unmappedTarget.text: according as I said to you
unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV includes this saying-reference clause, placed here from the longer TR reading at 10:26; the clause is absent from pinned N1904 10:26–27, so there are no raw Greek words here to anchor it.

10:28.sourceText: κἀγὼ δίδωμι αὐτοῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀπόλωνται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, καὶ οὐχ ἁρπάσει τις αὐτὰ ἐκ τῆς χειρός μου.
10:28.targetText: and I give continuous life to them, and they will not perish—throughout the age, and no one will snatch them out of My hand;

10:29.sourceText: ὁ Πατήρ μου ὃ δέδωκέν μοι πάντων μεῖζόν ἐστιν, καὶ οὐδεὶς δύναται ἁρπάζειν ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ Πατρός.
10:29.targetText: My Father, who has given to Me, is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch out of the hand of My Father;

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness/relative difference: N1904 ὃ is neuter what/that which, referring to what the Father has given; LSV who follows masculine ὃς referring to the Father. These relative pronouns do not have the same grammatical referent.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness/relative difference: LSV who refers to the Father; pinned N1904 has neuter ὃ (what He has given), not that masculine relative.
Source witness/explicit possessive difference: LSV repeats My at the final Father reference; N1904 τοῦ Πατρός has no repeated μου pronoun.

review.note: N1904 uses neuter ὃ and μεῖζον, making what the Father has given the grammatical greater-than-all subject; LSV uses the masculine Father-relative reading. Shared Father/give/greater lexemes are retained, while the incompatible relative is unpaired and the different comparative agreement and clause subject are explicit.

10:30.sourceText: ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἕν ἐσμεν.
10:30.targetText: I and the Father are one.”

10:31.sourceText: Ἐβάστασαν πάλιν λίθους οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἵνα λιθάσωσιν αὐτόν.
10:31.targetText: Therefore, again, the Jews took up stones that they may stone Him;

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV begins Therefore; N1904 has no οὖν or corresponding inferential connective in this verse.

10:32.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πολλὰ ἔργα ἔδειξα ὑμῖν καλὰ ἐκ τοῦ Πατρός· διὰ ποῖον αὐτῶν ἔργον ἐμὲ λιθάζετε;
10:32.targetText: Jesus answered them, “I showed you many good works from My Father; because of which work of them do you stone Me?”

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV qualifies Father with My; pinned N1904 has τοῦ Πατρός without μου in this verse.

10:33.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Περὶ καλοῦ ἔργου οὐ λιθάζομέν σε ἀλλὰ περὶ βλασφημίας, καὶ ὅτι σὺ ἄνθρωπος ὢν ποιεῖς σεαυτὸν Θεόν.
10:33.targetText: The Jews answered Him, saying, “We do not stone You for a good work, but for slander, and because You, being a man, make Yourself God.”

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness/explicit speech-marker difference: LSV includes saying after answered Him; N1904 begins the direct answer without a corresponding λέγοντες participle.

10:34.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐκ ἔστιν γεγραμμένον ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ὑμῶν ὅτι Ἐγὼ εἶπα Θεοί ἐστε;
10:34.targetText: Jesus answered them, “Is it not having been written in your law: I said, you are gods?

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the Scripture quotation; LSV uses punctuation and direct speech without a separate English that.

10:35.sourceText: εἰ ἐκείνους εἶπεν θεοὺς πρὸς οὓς ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐγένετο, καὶ οὐ δύναται λυθῆναι ἡ γραφή,
10:35.targetText: If He called them gods to whom the word of God came (and the Writing is not able to be broken),

10:36.sourceText: ὃν ὁ Πατὴρ ἡγίασεν καὶ ἀπέστειλεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι Βλασφημεῖς, ὅτι εἶπον Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰμι;
10:36.targetText: of Him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, do you say—You slander, because I said, I am [the] Son of God?

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: the first ὅτι introduces the charge You slander; LSV gives direct speech without a separate that. The later ὅτι is explicitly because.

unmappedTarget.reason: Translation addition: LSV supplies a bracketed article before Son; N1904 Υἱός is anarthrous in this clause.

10:37.sourceText: εἰ οὐ ποιῶ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Πατρός μου, μὴ πιστεύετέ μοι·
10:37.targetText: If I do not do the works of My Father, do not believe Me;

10:38.sourceText: εἰ δὲ ποιῶ, κἂν ἐμοὶ μὴ πιστεύητε, τοῖς ἔργοις πιστεύετε, ἵνα γνῶτε καὶ γινώσκητε ὅτι ἐν ἐμοὶ ὁ Πατὴρ κἀγὼ ἐν τῷ Πατρί.
10:38.targetText: and if I do, even if you may not believe Me, believe the works, that you may know and may believe that the Father [is] in Me, and I in Him.”

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness verb difference: N1904 γινώσκητε is a knowing verb (you may know/continue knowing); LSV may believe follows the believing-verb reading. The different knowing and believing lexemes are not equated.
Source witness/explicit referent difference: N1904 names τῷ Πατρί (the Father) after in; LSV instead uses the pronoun Him. No exact noun/pronoun lexical identity is asserted.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness verb difference: LSV may believe corresponds to πιστεύσητε, not N1904 γινώσκητε (know).
Source witness/explicit referent difference: LSV uses Him at the end; pinned N1904 explicitly names the Father there.
Translation addition: LSV supplies a bracketed copula in the Father-in-Me nominal clause; N1904 has no finite copula at that point.

10:39.sourceText: Ἐζήτουν οὖν αὐτὸν πάλιν πιάσαι· καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν.
10:39.targetText: Therefore they were seeking again to seize Him, and He went forth out of their hand,

10:40.sourceText: Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πάλιν πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου εἰς τὸν τόπον ὅπου ἦν Ἰωάνης τὸ πρῶτον βαπτίζων, καὶ ἔμενεν ἐκεῖ.
10:40.targetText: and went away again to the other side of the Jordan, to the place where John was at first immersing, and remained there,

10:41.sourceText: καὶ πολλοὶ ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἰωάνης μὲν σημεῖον ἐποίησεν οὐδέν, πάντα δὲ ὅσα εἶπεν Ἰωάνης περὶ τούτου ἀληθῆ ἦν.
10:41.targetText: and many came to Him and said, “John, indeed, did no sign, and all things, as many as John said about this One were true”;

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the direct observation about John; LSV uses direct speech without a separate that.

10:42.sourceText: καὶ πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν ἐκεῖ.
10:42.targetText: and many believed in Him there.
